findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler cannot be instantiated: abstract methods not implemented
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (abstract) but only contains `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler declares several abstract members that must be implemented: `counter_names` (abstract property), `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the newly-added `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Since none of these are overridden, attempting to instantiate this handler (e.g. via `Detector.detector_handler` -> `group_type.detector_handler(self)`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Previously this class had a concrete (stub) `evaluate` method and worked fine when instantiated; this change silently breaks that contract. Any code path that resolves a Detector of type `metric_alert_fire` and tries to use its handler will crash.

findings.title: Stale comment after switching base class
findings.body: The comment `# TODO: This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction` is left in place even though the class now already inherits from `StatefulDetectorHandler`. The comment is now inaccurate/misleading and should be removed or updated to reflect that the handler is stateful but still unimplemented.

findings.title: Unused logger after removing duplicate-group-key error logging
findings.body: The duplicate detection code in `process_detectors` that previously used `logger.error(...)` to report duplicate group keys was removed as part of switching `evaluate()` to return a dict. The module-level `logger` instance at line 30 is now unused anywhere in this file, which is dead code and may trip lint/static-analysis checks (unused variable).

findings.title: No regression test covers MetricAlertDetectorHandler instantiation
findings.body: The PR changes `StatefulDetectorHandler` to require implementing `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (and other abstract members), and updates `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` to subclass it with only `pass`. No test in this PR (or elsewhere visible) instantiates `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` or calls `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector of type `metric_alert_fire`, so the resulting `TypeError` on instantiation (due to unimplemented abstract methods) goes undetected by the test suite.
